Wording is mine, from the document; occurrences, surfaces, Strong's codes, morph codes and collections are looked up from verse_lexical and the live collections. NODE SELECTION RULE USED, AND ITS LIMIT: a node is placed on every occurrence of a unit-2 word (the dread and trembling words the ledger is about) in the verses the finding cites, role characteristic. That is mechanical. It does not node the other collection words the document names (a seat such as the heart, the party, the object), and it does not judge each role. A real re-read would. Roles are therefore inferential. max_verse_words_copied is 7.

new_observations.ledger_title: Dread before God's presence, voice, word and act
new_observations.obs_text: Dread and trembling arise before God himself: before his presence, his voice in the thunder, his word and his acts. Job is terrified at his presence and could not face his majesty; the camp at Sinai trembles; Daniel's companions flee and Daniel is left trembling; Joseph's brothers turn to one another in fear at what God has done; sinners in Zion ask who can live beside the consuming fire.

new_observations.ledger_title: Making others afraid, as an act
new_observations.obs_text: Fear is also done to others as an act, with the one who frightens as the subject: Ahithophel's plan to throw the king's company into a panic, Gideon throwing an army into panic, sorceries from which Babylon hopes to inspire terror, God's justice so that man may strike terror no more, creditors roused to make the debtor tremble, Job asking whether God will frighten a driven leaf, those sent to terrify the nations.

new_observations.ledger_title: Do not be in dread, with its ground
new_observations.obs_text: 'Do not be in dread' is spoken with its ground beside it: the Lord is in their midst, goes with them, or has said it from of old. The same word is turned to oneself as trust: I will not be afraid, whom shall I fear.

'None shall make you afraid' is the promise of peace: lying down in the land, sitting under the vine and fig tree, dwelling securely, returning in quiet, being led in safety; Zophar offers it to Job as the outcome of turning.

The dread root appears in joy: the heart thrills and exults, and the people fear and tremble because of all the good and the prosperity provided for them after their guilt is forgiven, alongside rejoicing with trembling.

new_observations.ledger_title: The earth, mountains, heavens, waters and the dead tremble
new_observations.obs_text: The physical world and the dead tremble before God, with the words used of people: mountains quake at his anger, the deep trembles when the waters see him, the pillars of heaven tremble at his rebuke, the dead tremble under the waters, and the land trembles at those who trample the needy.

new_observations.ledger_title: One root, ragaz, rendered as trembling, rage, quarrel and grief
new_observations.obs_text: One Hebrew root, ragaz, 'to tremble', is rendered in the ESV as trembling, anger, raging, quarrelling, grief and disturbance: peoples and earth tremble, the psalmist is told to be angry and not sin, Sennacherib is said to have raged against God, Joseph tells his brothers not to quarrel, David is deeply moved at Absalom's death, Samuel is disturbed at being brought up, Sheol is stirred up.
